# Decisions — project decisions with rationale

### Branch from origin/main, switch to a derived branch

<!-- id=DEC-001, date=2026-04-01, tags=branch main, trigger=creating a feature branch, status=active -->

The default branch is `main` (not `master`). `bin/gh-branch <issue>` fetches
`origin/main` and creates `<type>/issue-<n>-<slug>` from it. If the branch
already exists locally or on origin, it switches to it instead of failing.
A dirty tree on `main` aborts creation unless `--force` is given. `main` is
**not** PR-protected by a ruleset (unlike workerman-bundle's `master`), but
direct pushes to `main` are still forbidden by the workflow — always use a PR.

### Conventional commits with scope

<!-- id=DEC-002, date=2026-04-01, tags=commits, trigger=writing a commit message, status=active -->

Commit messages follow `<type>(<scope>): <subject> (closes #<n>)`. Types:
`feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `refactor`, `ci`, `test`, `chore`, `perf`, `build`.
Scopes map to `src/` subdirectories or top-level concerns: `(encoding)`,
`(renderer)`, `(exception)`,`(composer)`, `(ffi)`, `(config)`, `(core)`,
`(ci)`, `(process)`. Reference the issue with `(closes #<n>)` on the
implementation commit so GitHub auto-closes it on merge.

### composer.lock is not committed

<!-- id=DEC-004, date=2026-04-01, tags=lock, trigger=question about whether to commit composer.lock, status=active -->

`composer.lock` is in `.gitignore` and is intentionally not tracked. This is
a library (type `composer-plugin`), not an application: consumers resolve
their own versions. Do not commit `composer.lock` and do not remove it from
`.gitignore`. CI runs `composer install` fresh on each leg.

### CI runs PHPUnit across PHP 8.2–8.4

<!-- id=DEC-003, date=2026-04-01, tags=ci, trigger=adding a CI job or changing the matrix, status=active -->

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs a permission check, then a PHP 8.2–8.4 matrix
that builds the C++ FFI library and runs `composer test`. PHP 8.1 was dropped:
PHPUnit ^11.5 and Paratest ^7.6 require PHP 8.2+. The precompiled `.so`
binaries are still built for 8.1 in `release-build.yml` (a compiled extension
links against the 8.1 ABI), but the PHP code in `src/` requires 8.2+. There is
no aggregator `ci` job and no required-status ruleset. Lint jobs (phpstan,
php-cs-fixer, rector) are part of the workflow tooling (`composer lint`) but
are **not** wired into CI yet — run `composer lint` locally before opening a
PR until CI lint jobs are added.

### PHPStan level 4 with a baseline; lint via composer scripts

<!-- id=DEC-005, date=2026-04-01, tags=lint phpstan baseline, trigger=adding or relaxing a static-analysis rule, status=active -->

`composer lint` runs php-cs-fixer (dry-run), phpstan, rector (dry-run) and
`bin/kb-lint.php`; `composer lint-fix` applies the fixable ones. PHPStan runs
at **level 4** with `phpstan-baseline.neon` carrying the pre-existing debt
counted when the workflow was introduced (76 errors, all false positives from
PHPUnit already-narrowed assertions and `*NEVER*` QR-matrix range reasoning in
`FastEncoder`/`MaskSelector`). The baseline is committed so the floor is
stable: a new PR that adds a level-4 violation fails `composer lint`, while
old violations are tracked until they are fixed and removed from the baseline.
The goal is to raise the level and shrink the baseline over time; lowering the
level or deleting baseline entries to make a round look clean is forbidden
(see workflow `§6`). `src/NativeEncoder.php` and `src/FfiEncoder.php` are
excluded from analysis — the first is a conditional `if/else` class
declaration that swaps in a C core when `extension_loaded('scanmeqr')`, the
second is an FFI boundary using `FFI::cdef` dynamic C struct properties and
functions; PHPStan cannot resolve either statically.

### Consumer-pinned SHA-256 checksums are the trust anchor for native binary downloads

<!-- id=DEC-006, date=2026-08-18, tags=security composer ffi, trigger=proposing a fallback to the installed package's own composer.json for checksums, or questioning why composer install refuses to download binaries, status=active -->

The Composer plugin (`src/Composer/Plugin.php`) routes all native binary
downloads through `BinaryDownloader::download()`, which is **fail-closed**: if
no SHA-256 checksum can be determined it throws
`DownloadException::checksumMissing()` before any HTTP request or file
creation. Checksums are read from the **consumer's root** `composer.json`
(`extra.scanmephp.checksums`), resolved via
`dirname($composer->getConfig()->get('vendor-dir'))` — NOT the package's own
`vendor/crazy-goat/scanmephp/composer.json`. An attacker who takes over the
release channel can swap the binary AND the package's own composer.json, but
NOT the consumer's root composer.json. Do not add a vendor-package checksum
fallback — it defeats the entire fix (#48 / PR #181). Verification happens
before `chmod 0755`. Signature verification (minisign/cosign) is a known
future enhancement (#182); a consumer-pinned digest does not fully protect
against org-account takeover. On-disk binaries are re-verified against the
pinned checksum since #185 (PR #192): `ChecksumManager::existingBinaryIsValid()`
is fail-closed when a checksum is pinned (mismatch or unhashable → unlink and
re-download through the verified path), while the no-checksum legacy
acceptance is preserved for consumers without pinned checksums.
